newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese lawyers tell pope Christian persecuted.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese lawyers tell pope Christian persecuted.

text.p: Lawyers for jailed Christian warlord Samir Geagea told Pope John Paul on Monday he was being persecuted by the authorities because Lebanon had failed to achieve reconciliation between Christians and Moslems since the 1975-90 civil war.

"We...express our deep concern about the continuous persecution of our client Samir Geagea," the three lawyers said in an open letter to the pope published in Beirut newspapers six days before he starts a two-day visit to Lebanon.
"He (Geagea) has been held for more than 1,100 days in a narrow underground cell where he is deprived of sunlight, fresh air, correspondence, company and access to the media," the lawyers said.
Geagea headed the main Christian militia, the Lebanese Forces, during the war and is the only former Lebanese warlord to have been put on trial.
He twice refused to join postwar pro-Syrian governments and was arrested in 1994 and his group outlawed when he was accused of carrying out a church bombing in which 11 people died.
A court found him not guilty for lack of evidence but he has since been tried for three other murders and sentenced to three life terms in jail.
Geagea will be sentenced on Friday in a fourth case -- an alleged murder attempt on Michel al-Murr, a Christian politician who is now interior minister and deputy prime minister.

Cardinal Nasrallah Sfeir, Lebanon's Maronite patriarch, has repeatedly protested that Geagea is the only former sectarian warlord to have been tried and has complained of sectarian bias by the authorities.
Several other former sectarian warlords are in the government of billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri or hold high office.
Geagea's lawyers complained that the government had failed to implement the 1989 Taef agreement on national reconciliation that brought the civil war to an end.
"Until now, reconciliation has not taken place among the Lebanese and domestic peace has not been achieved, and that hurts the unity of the country," they said in their letter to the pope.
"We address you, asking your blessing on national reconciliation, the achievement of domestic peace and equality among the Lebanese," they added.
